messages:
maria: quick heads-up 1: i've consolidated a refreshed incident communications kit. aim: one canonical set of short templates for on-call posts, status-page copy, customer emails, and support canned replies. sharing draft here for review before i open a PR. please flag any phrases that sound too legal or promise-y.

sanjay: thanks. can we include a parsable severity field in the header (S1/S2) so downstream tooling can auto-tag? also call out preferred timestamp format (ISO UTC).

maria: adding `Severity: {{S1|S2}}` and a note: times should be `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`. main design goals: short, factual, separate "what we know" and "what we don't know", explicit owners on mitigations, and an on-call handoff snippet.

elaine: support keeps guessing at root cause in ticket replies. please include a vetted single-sentence placeholder for unknown-cause replies.

kevin: candidate neutral line: "Root cause is under investigation; we will confirm scope and next steps as soon as available." short and safe.

maria: adding kevin's line into the templates. here's the INTERNAL #incidents message template (single-message, paste-ready):

```
Incident {{incident_id}} | Severity: {{S1|S2}} | {{service_name}}
Summary: {{one_line_summary}}
What we know: {{known_facts}}
Open / unknowns: {{unknowns}}
Impact (customers): ~{{percent}}% or {{segments}}; symptom: {{symptom}}
Actions in progress:
 - {{action_1}} (owner: @{{owner1}})
 - {{action_2}} (owner: @{{owner2}})
Mitigation / Workaround: {{workaround_if_any}}
Next update ETA: {{minutes}} min
Handoff (current -> next): @{{current_oncall}} -> @{{next_oncall}}; notes: {{handoff_notes}}
Links: {{logs}} | {{traces}} | {{incident_doc_link}}
TL;DR (one line): {{service_name}} degraded 96 partial impact; mitigation in progress. Details: {{incident_doc_link}}
```

mira: minor nit: include a short `Validated by:` line when someone confirms mitigation. prevents duplicate checks.

maria: good call 1. adding `Validated by: @{{validator}}` under mitigations.

maria: PUBLIC STATUS PAGE SNIPPETS (pick one, keep short):

Public - baseline (status page, first post):
```
We are experiencing degraded performance for {{service_name}}. Engineers are investigating and working to restore normal operation. We will provide updates every {{interval}} minutes on this page.
```

Public - mitigation applied (status page update):
```
A mitigation has been applied for {{service_name}} and systems are being validated. Some customers may still see intermittent issues while we confirm full recovery. Next update by {{next_update}}.
```

maria: CUSTOMER-FACING EMAIL (high-touch template):

```
Subject: Incident {{incident_id}} affecting {{service_name}}
Hi {{customer_name}},
We're investigating an issue affecting {{feature}} which may cause {{symptom}}. Our engineers have applied mitigations and are monitoring results. Next update: {{next_update}}. For urgent assistance please contact {{support_link}} or reply to this message and we'll escalate to your account team.
Regards,
Redwood Support
```

elaine: for enterprise customers add a short escalation path and their TAM/contact name when applicable. keeps them calm.

kevin: SUPPORT CANNED RESPONSES (two sizes):
- Acknowledge: "Thanks for the report 96 we're investigating and will update you shortly."
- Update for tickets: "We're actively mitigating an issue affecting {{feature}}. Current status: {{status}}. Next update: {{next_update}}. Support: {{support_link}}."

luke: social / comms team snippet: "We're aware of reports about {{service_name}} and are investigating. Updates will be posted to our status page." no technical detail, no SLA talk.

maria: HANDOFF CHECKLIST (copyable block):

```
Handoff checklist:
- 1-2 line current status summary
- Open actions + owners (who will do what)
- Mitigations applied + who validated them (Validated by: @username)
- Known impact: segments / percent / customer examples
- Key links: logs | traces | runbook | status page
- Next update ETA
```

sanjay: add a short 'on-call notes' field for environment-sensitive details (e.g., regions affected, model variants).

maria: added `On-call notes: {{env_notes}}`.

maria: DO / DO NOT quick guidance (one-paragraph each):
Do: use plain language, quantify impact when possible, include next update ETA, attach links to logs/traces.
Do not: claim "no data loss" or offer credits without engineering/legal/finance sign-off; avoid definitive root-cause claims; do not promise exact time-to-fix.

kevin: please include a short approved-boilerplate list for quick copy-paste in Slack or email.

maria: approved boilerplates (copy-paste):
- "We're investigating and will update shortly."
- "Mitigation in progress; next update in {{minutes}} minutes."
- "Mitigation applied; validating recovery."

maria: examples of phrases to avoid (for the playbook):
- "No data was lost" (unless confirmed by engineering + legal)
- "We will issue credits" (needs finance sign-off)
- "Issue resolved" (avoid until validated end-to-end)

incident-bot: [automated] reminder: when you publish customer-facing text, update the public status page and the #incidents channel. Use `/status-update` to push changes.

maria: operational plan: i'll assemble a single markdown `docs/incidents/comm-templates.md` with these blocks, include a short changelog and callouts for legal/finance review where necessary. PR owner: maria; reviewers: sanjay, kevin; publisher: tara. target: PR opened by EOD.

kevin: i'll smoke-test templates with incident-bot rendering and validate codeblocks survive Slack -> docs conversion.

mira: i'll prep two fully filled example incidents (one S1, one S2) so we can sanity-check copy and that the TL;DR fits within cross-channel limits.

elaine: i'll paste two enterprise email variants in this thread in ~30m for inclusion.

maria: final q for the group: should we include a 3-question FAQ template for post-incident comms? (what happened, who was impacted, next steps/timeframe for RCA).

sanjay: yes, short FAQ helps reduce ticket repeat. include placeholders for RCA ETA.

maria: noted. i'll add a tiny FAQ snippet to the PR. thanks all 1. tagging @incident-bot to remind the on-call channel once the PR merges.

incident-bot: [automated] noted 96 will ping #oncall after `docs/incidents/comm-templates.md` merges to encourage adoption."
